title: Skip key copy in untyped Dictionary accessors

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Every `Dictionary` accessor (`operator[]`, `getptr`, `get`, `get_valid`, `get_or_add`, `set`, `has`, `has_all`, `erase`) starts with `Variant key = p_key;`, copying the key so it can be passed to `typed_key.validate()`, which takes a non-const reference and may coerce the key for typed dictionaries.

For an untyped dictionary (`typed_key.type == Variant::NIL`, the common case) `validate()` returns immediately without touching the key, so that copy is pure overhead. When the key is a `String`, `StringName`, `Array` or any `RefCounted`, the copy is an atomic refcount round-trip on every access.

This adds an untyped fast path to each accessor that uses `p_key` directly and skips the copy and the no-op validation. Typed dictionaries are unchanged: they still take the existing path and coerce keys exactly as before. Value handling is untouched.

### Benchmark

Fixed-key tight loop from a `SceneTree` script, 8M iterations, best-of-5, release editor build, same machine (Windows, x86_64). Numbers include GDScript VM overhead, so the accessor-level improvement is a larger share than the wall-clock delta below.

| operation | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| string-key read (`dict[k]`) | 202 ns/op | 188 ns/op |
| string-key write (`dict[k] = v`) | 181 ns/op | 164 ns/op |
| string-key `k in dict` | 299 ns/op | 279 ns/op |
| int-key read | 251 ns/op | 247 ns/op |
| int-key `k in dict` | 246 ns/op | 237 ns/op |

String keys benefit most (the removed atomic refcount traffic); integer keys still save the `Variant` construct/destruct.

### Correctness

A GDScript check script exercises String/StringName key equivalence, `get`/`get_valid`/`get_or_add`/`erase`/`has_all`, read-only rejection, and typed-dictionary key coercion (float coerced to int) and value handling. All assertions pass on the patched build.
